utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, good afternoon to you. Could you call the case, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. All the accused are present. From the Defence teams I notice the absence of Mr. Ostojic, Madam Nikolic, Mr. Lazarevic and Mr. Haynes and Mr. Krgovic. I understand that the Popovic Defence team has got some kind of preliminary.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, thank you very much. I will be very brief. In the course of the morning we received an e-mail from the Prosecution which is relative to today's witness, who took a solemn declaration yesterday but we cannot contact him. In their e-mail they inform us about their approach to the document. We believe that we are actually taken by surprise because we cannot verify with our witness the allegations about the quality of that document. In any case we are going to tender this document into evidence once his examination-in-chief is over. This is as much as we wanted to inform the Trial Chamber about, to tell them that we are not in a position to verify the information with the witness. I would like to introduce our intern who is present in the courtroom today, Ms. Liane Aronchick who is going to join us in the courtroom today, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. [Microphone not activated] welcome, Madam. As regards your submission, Madam Tapuskovic, I must confess I didn't quite understand what this is all about. We are not, of course, privy to the exchange of correspondence that went on between the Prosecution and you. We don't know what document you are referring to and what is the problem if there is a problem. If either you or someone from the Prosecution could explain a little bit further, we would be in a better position to direct you as to the best way possible to proceed forward.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you very much. The document in question is a document, very important both for the Defence and the Prosecution. This is a list of displaced persons which is very important for the conclusions of the witness and of the Defence and we received information from the Prosecution that this document bears a different name according to their database. But we believe that the evidence is absolutely reliable and that's why we are going to tender it into the Defence evidence and we are going to examine the witness about that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Do you wish to comment, Ms. Soljan, do you wish to comment?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Just briefly, Your Honours. I don't think we are going to object to this proposal but it has to do with an MIFing issue that has to do with a description of document issue that came to our attention when we were reviewing these documents. I don't think we will be objecting. We don't think it's significant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's deal with it, if at all, when it arises, if it arises as a problem. Otherwise we won't need to deal with it. Anything else? Let's bring the witness in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And welcome back. We are resuming your expert evidence today. Madam Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: We will continue where we left it off yesterday in your examination-in-chief. When you were talking about the application of the criteria, in your paper, in paragraph 16, you mention the application of the conservative criterion. Could you please explain to the Trial Chamber the notion of the conservative criterion?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my report -- actually it is Brunborg and Urdal's report that I'm talking about where the conservative criterion is mentioned as a procedure or as the continued procedure to identify the missing persons on the consolidated list of missing persons in the census. The report does not provide any further explanation of that criterion. However it may be understood from the contents that it is a subjective criterion which implies evaluation on the part of the expert as to whether a pair, which had been found to match the 71 criteria should be adopted or rejected.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Brunborg and his associate Henrik Urdal anywhere in their report provide the reasons why some pairs had to be rejected and some not?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We don't have any documents to that effect. The process of identification of certain persons from the list of missing with the census or the list of voters has not been explained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Madam Tapuskovic. Yes, Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you Your Honours. Just for the sake of the clarity of the record again, I would like to make sure we know what exact report we are referring to right now. Is this the April 2000 report or is that something else? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Soljan. Yes, Ms. Tapuskovic. I think that's a fair comment. Would you address it, please, with the witness? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic, which report by Henrik Urdal and the main author of the author Mr. Brunborg does your comment refer to?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the report in front of me. The date is February 2000.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. When you were talking about the criteria for matching that Helge Brunborg applied, in your expert report you say that there is the extensivity of the composing of these matching criteria. Can you please tell us now what you meant by this extensivity in composing criteria?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I meant was the fact that in a number of these criteria, the author went from the most rigorous one to the least rigorous one so as to achieve the highest probability that a person on the list of missing will be found in the census, i.e., to completely reduce the possibility for a person not to be found. In addition to that, there are 57 persons that I've mentioned in my report in paragraph 14 that cannot be matched with any person in the census according to any of the criteria, and this is the element that points to that extensivity.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If I understand you well this means that when you performed your matching between the census and the Brunborg's list and when you applied all of these criteria, your result was 57 persons who could not be matched according to any of the criteria?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Let me repeat, there are 57 persons in the list of the missing persons that could not be matched according to any of the 71 criteria.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. How did you then understand Brunborg's approach to the identification of the missing persons? And I'm now talking about the census.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way I understood it was in the light of the 71 criteria as completely limitless with regard to the possibility to match a person on the list of the missing persons with the list that is the 1991 census. Obviously I could not reconstruct the whole procedure because we were not able to replicate the so-called conservative criterion.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, the procedure for matching between the list of the missing persons by Helge Brunborg the so-called consolidated list and the census, in any way, was it documented in Helge Brunborg's report in any way?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, yes, Ms. Soljan?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: I apologise to my learned counsel for interrupting again, but again I would like just clarification. When we are talking about the consolidated missing persons list by Helge Brunborg are we discussing the May 2000 list or are we discussing -- and that would be P566, or are we discussing the 16 November 2005 list, 2414?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Mr. Kovacevic, I am appealing to your cooperation here because I wouldn't like this to happen again and again. When either Ms. Tapuskovic refers you to a particular document, I understand that in your mind you would know exactly what you are referring to. If you could indicate that straight away to us so that there will be no confusion at all in anybody's mind as to which document either you or Ms. Tapuskovic or both of you are referring to, please? So I am going to leave it entirely in your hands from now on to start indicating which documents you are referring to from the Brunborg reports.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, all the time I've been talking about the so-called consolidated list of the missing persons that was compiled by Messrs. Brunborg and Urdal and the last version of that list was provided to us in the demographic department of this Tribunal. In other words, at the beginning, we mentioned the ICRC list and the physicians for human rights list that were used to compile the consolidated list, but from that moment on, we stopped talking about those two lists. We have been talking only about the consolidated list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I still don't think this answers the question because the list from 2000 contains 7.475 missing persons. The list that we have, the most recent list is the 7.661 missing. I just want to make sure that we are discussing this most recent one that reflects the 7.661. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Would you confirm that, Mr. Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And in many places in my report, the figure of 7.661 is mentioned, and this consolidated list was provided to us in April of this year in the demographic unit. I do not refer to the original list which has since been extended, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Kovacevic, for this useful explanation. Let's now go back to where we left it off. I'll repeat my question. Let's go back to the criteria in one of the paragraphs of your report, you indicate that the criteria were relaxed and that several procedures to that effect were applied. What procedures are you talking about? How does one relax the criteria?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The criteria were devised in such a way so as to start from a unique key that I have already mentioned, I did it in my testimony yesterday, and this key contains the first name, the last name, the father's name, the sex, the date and place of birth, and then by the process of reduction of the identifying elements in various combinations, one would arrive at those criteria starting with the most stringent to the least stringent criteria.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And now I would kindly ask for 3D368 to be brought up in e-court. Mr. Kovacevic, you're going to see on your screen, on the right-hand side, this document, and you will please tell us what the document represents. Can we scroll down a little? To the end of the page? Do you see the table, Mr. Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you -- can we now move to the next page, please? Mr. Kovacevic, what kind of a document is this, the one what you're looking at on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document that provides a very exact formula or articulates exactly the 71 criteria.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us which of the criteria, as you said it yourself is the most relaxed one, and which provides the biggest possibility for the candidates to be found for the persons who are listed in the list of missing persons?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously, you can't explain it in very simple terms, especially not on the basis of this document. However, based on the analysis and processing that we carried out, by using each of these criteria to match the list of the missing persons with the census, it is obviously criterion number 42. If you scroll down a little, then you will see this criterion, number 42, yes, thank you. Criterion 42 calls for a match between the initial of the first name, the initial of the last name, the initial of father's name, and the year of birth, and that year of birth can differ by plus or minus three years.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And now I would like to call up 1D1129 in e-court, please. And can we please display page number 6 in the B/C/S version and in the English version the table starts on page 5 and continues on page 6. Let's look at criterion 42 that you have just spoken about, Mr. Kovacevic. Can we scroll down just a little bit more? Down. Thank you. Mr. Kovacevic, do you see on the screen the table which is overview 1 from your report?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, in the second and third columns, what are these figures? What do they represent in the light of what you have just told us about the 42nd criterion?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the second column, we have number 118032, which is the number of persons in the census who could be matched with some of the individuals on the list of missing persons according to this criterion. The third column, this number of 118032 has been reduced to 6.958. This was done in the following way. For each of the persons, only one matching was taken into account, and I'm talking about the list of missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Does it mean that for 6.958 persons for the list of missing persons, we have 180.032 candidates in the census?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That means that for 7.661 persons from the list of missing persons, we have 180.032 candidates in the census and the number of 6.958 represents the group of people in the census which correspond to some of the persons on the list of missing persons according to just one criterion.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When talking about a consolidated list of the missing persons, can you tell me which were the most frequent shortcomings you've encountered on that list?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we are talking about the list of the missing persons, and in view of the comparisons with the census, the most frequent shortcomings or deficiencies appear with dates of birth, place of disappearance and place of birth. Of course, there are also deficiencies in terms of first and last names, father's name, et cetera, but to a lesser degree.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The deficiencies or the shortcomings, could they have been compensated for in any way?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we trust the list of the missing persons, then those -- that information could have been supplied from the census.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You say they could have been supplied in that way. Do you have an explanation as to why this was not done?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not, because the procedure of documenting the relations in the triangle consisting of the census, the list of missing and the voters' register was not applied.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what would be your final belief concerning the trustworthiness of the list of the missing persons compiled by Helge Brunborg?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the research I carried out, the intention to prove that each of the persons from the list existed is evident, as is the intention that each and every single one of those persons went missing, i.e. that that person is no longer among the living on the voters' list.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You provided your opinion concerning the Brunborg criteria. Can you tell us this: Which criterion that can be used for matching would be something that you would be able to accept from the consolidated list of the missing persons and the census?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the existing information from the census and the list, a sensible criteria would be the following. It would have to contain first, last name, father's name and year of birth.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us why one needs to have the year of birth instead of a date of birth?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because a date of birth, as frequently happens and we can see that in one of the tables, for example in paragraph 26, it is frequently missing from the list of the missing persons. However, we often have the year of birth. The criterion I propose contains the maximum number of elements with the information that appears with the most frequency in both sources.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If we are to apply this sensible criterion, as you called it, containing first and last name, father's name and year of birth, what would be the result of matching the information from the consolidated list of the missing persons and the census?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is stated in paragraph 27. Such matching provides us with a list of 2.943 people.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What would be the status of those persons?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me? I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You said that in paragraph 27, we have a list of 2943 missing persons. That is to say that was the result of matching the information from the list of the missing persons and the census?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your report and yesterday you mentioned the existence of the personal identification number, the JMBG applied to every citizens as a unique identifier. In your methodological notes to your report and in paragraph 23, you mentioned the JMBG. Can you tell us what it comprised and in what list did it exist?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The JMBG is an administrative code assigned to every person when registering the event of birth. It contains the whole date of birth plus an extension which provides for the uniqueness of the code. In the records we used for the research we came across the JMBG because it is contained in the voters' list and the census.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you verify the accuracy of the JMBGs?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We matched it with the census.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What were the results when verifying the accuracy of that information?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The census, of course, is not an administrative register but a statistical one, and of course some of the JMBGs therein were inaccurate. Concerning the census in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1991, some 32 people included -- 32 per cent of people included did not have their JMBG. The figure is 1.400.000. Usually after the date of birth, there were zeros, that is to say the extension was missing that should have provided for the uniqueness of the code.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What were the results of matching, as you stated in paragraph 24, what were the results of the matching you carried out?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in paragraph 24, it is stated that 57 people from the missing persons list could not be matched based on any of Brunborg rules. That's what I've already mentioned when we talked about the criteria.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You carried out this matching procedure according to the 71 criteria using the consolidated list of the missing persons and the voters' registers?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What were the results of matching of that type, using the consolidated list of the missing persons and the voters' registers?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to make such matching possible, according to the criteria, we copied the name of the father, when available, from the census into the voters' register. According to Brunborg's information, the fact that many fathers' names were missing and that is why they did not use the same criteria to match the two documents as they did against the census. When we did that, we matched 6983 persons from the list of the missing persons against the voters' registers in 1997, 1998. According to these criteria, we were unable to match 678 persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What strikes you as characteristic when talking about the matching between the list of the missing persons and the voters' register which is something you discuss in paragraph 26?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is characteristic that when we use a relatively stringent or a very stringent criterion to match the list of the missing persons with the voters' register, and that is the criterion containing name, last name, father's name and year of birth, we end up with 22 persons who were present on both lists. An interesting point which we do not find in the Brunborg report would be is -- is to ask why these people were not taken into account as someone who could have been in the voters' register, that is to say people who were not on the list of the missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Using the same exhibit, 1D1129, I would now like to go to page 8, in order to be able to see the table or the result you mentioned, i.e. the 22 persons. Could you please show us the next page, to see the end of the table? This is the beginning. Mr. Kovacevic, you identified in absolute terms which are the persons appearing on both lists for which we can say that they were -- that they could be on the list of the missing persons as well as alive.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on this, we cannot say with any degree of certainty that those people are alive, but we can say that the 22 persons, using a relatively stringent criterion, can be found on both the list of the missing persons and in the voters' register and that the criterion, the conservative criterion, which is extraordinarily stringent, eliminated these persons as those being potentially present on the voters' register, that is to say alive, possibly alive, at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In several paragraphs you mentioned the importance of the number of 3.000, that is to say the result of your research which did not result in the numbers greater than 3.000. Can you tell us why the figure of 3.000 is so characteristic?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on cross-referencing several sources, and based on -- and based on the contrasting of the same sources, on several occasions I came up with a figure close to 3.000, which was indicative. When I say indicative, I mean that with a degree of possibility, one could believe that that is the real number of missing. I will cite six examples. I've already mentioned one when we were matching the Brunborg list, that is the list of the missing persons that we have been discussing all along, against census with the criterion of first and last name and year of birth and the figure obtained was 2943. Another indicative figure was arrived at by matching the Brunborg list of the missing persons with the list of killed soldiers of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, going by their first and last name, name of one of the parents and year of birth. The figure obtained in that way is concluded with 2.743 persons. The third indicator is the following: When we use the number of soldiers in Srebrenica, which is 6.000, according to a document concerning the military forces in Srebrenica, and when we deduct from that figure the figure of survived soldiers from Srebrenica which is 3105, we arrive at the figure of 2805. The fourth indication is the following, and it has a separate chapter, separate paragraph in the report. If we take the population of Srebrenica and deduct the number of displaced persons from Srebrenica, we arrive at a figure which is less than 2989. The fifth indicative figure is the following. If we use the number of identified persons, which is 3947, using the original list after duplicates have been eliminated, if we from that figure deduct the number of those who were killed by early 1995, which is 1300, we arrive at 2647. The sixth indicative figure is something we received by matching the Brunborg list, the list of the missing persons, with the list of identified persons, and then we arrive at a figure of 2.738.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All the figures you mentioned, and I believe there were six, when they are compared with the number of the missing persons on the consolidated list of Helge Brunborg, what is your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First and foremost, my conclusion would be a purely statistical one. That is to say that all these figures are in the area of 3.000, the figure being rather indicative or characteristic. It is far less than 7.661 [Realtime transcript read in error "6.661"]. These indicators bring into question the 7.661 figure that is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kovacevic. Let us move on to the second part of your report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Tapuskovic, could you check the number with the witness which appears on line 5, the figure is -- we arrived at the end of the day, 2.738? Just for clarity.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The number indeed is 2.738.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we also have an intervention about the record, page 16, line 12, it says 6.661 and it should be 7.661.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I may have misspoken.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic, what's the correct number, just to correct the figure in the record? What is the correct number of people that are listed on Brunborg's list?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7.661. And this is the number that I've been talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to chapter 12 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: -- in your report, and let's go to page 10 in B/C/S version and page 8 in English version, and I'm talking about this document that we already have on the screen which is 1D1129. Mr. Kovacevic, in your report, what is the significance of the chapter entitled, "Statistical evidence on the unsustainability of Brunborg's list"?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The part of the report under this title, which is statistical evidence of the unsustainability of Brunborg's list and 7.661 missing persons, represents a statistical analysis of all the available data based on the available documents, i.e. data sources, and the adequate relations which were used in order to establish the trustworthiness of the established number of missing persons on Brunborg's list, which is 7.661.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This table --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Soljan?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: In the course of his answers, the witness seems to be referring to multiple documents. I would like him to just identify what documents he's referring to while he's answering. Is it only his report or are there other documents that he's taking into consideration? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Ms. Soljan. Yes, Mr. Kovacevic, if could you explain that, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we are talking about this particular part of the report, and if we look at table 1, it is correct I'm talking about several documents. For example, in the first column, I'm talking about documents which provide the number of the population that existed before the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Soljan?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: I believe maybe the witness hasn't understood. It's not the explanation of the substance of his report that I'm referring to but the documents that he has before him right here in the witness stand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which documents are you referring to, Mr. Kovacevic, in your last answer, or the previous one, rather?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: From my point of view it's easier to see he has documents in both his right and left hand. I'm just curious what all those documents are basically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can't help you more than I have already. It's Mr. Kovacevic that has to explain this to us. Which documents are you referring to, Mr. Kovacevic? Which documents are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The document that we just started talking about is my report, and the title of this report, as you know, is expert report on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't read the title. We know that. Are you referring to also some other document that you have in front of you or just your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm also using my notes. I have extracted some of the things from my report in order to have all the figures handy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, there was another document and of course if they are his notes we would like to have access to those notes during break, at the latest. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Tapuskovic, perhaps you can explain that to your witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Maybe you can clarify with him if these are the only two documents he is using at the moments in answering the previous question or whether he's using even more than these two documents that he's mentioned and make it also clear that as soon as we have the break, he needs to make available his notes basically.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic, you heard the instruction provided by the Presiding Judge. Let me ask you, while you were providing your answers you have been using your report, as you said it. I'm very often referring to the chapters in your report. And you also told us you're using your personal notes, and when it comes to your personal notes, what do they contain? How many documents do you have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Currently, I have three documents. I have several documents in my binder, I have Brunborg's report, some other documents, rules, criteria. I have some documents that I used as the basis of my report.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Kovacevic. I hope that this is enough by way of explanation and I will follow the Trial Chamber's instruction in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Soljan?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Given the last thing that my learned friend has said, we would like to have access to the remaining two documents that the expert is referring to. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That will be done during the break if that is acceptable to you, Ms. Soljan, or do you insist on having it done now?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: The break is fine, thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if -- the witness said he is using different documents because of the figures because the witness himself said this is a statistical issue and that a lot of figures appear in his research, so one cannot reasonably expect from him to have all these figures in his head, and while he was compiling the report he used quite a lot of documents and the only way for him to testify is to use all these documents in order to be able to quote the exact figures. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic, let's go to table number 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Tapuskovic and Mr. Kovacevic, no one is criticising him for having brought notes or for trying to assist his own memory and his own testimony by means of notes. He's perfectly entitled to do that, but so is the Prosecution entitled to have access to them to verify that what he is saying is indeed what he is saying. Let's proceed anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic, let's look at table number 1, and let's look at column number 4. The number -- the name of that column is, number of missing, and in brackets, according to Brunborg's list. You've just told us that the total number of missing persons on the consolidated Brunborg's list is 7.661. Here, a different figure appears, 7.659. How do you account for the difference?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two persons appeared as duplicates when we did our IT search.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Using the same document, can we go to page 15 in B/C/S? Scroll down a little, please. Mr. Kovacevic, you have before you a table which, under items ID 6 and 7, mentions two persons. Can you say whether these are the two duplicates that you have just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about paragraph 49?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These are not the two cases. This is just an example showing how the consolidated list of identified persons was compiled. This is a different list and it says here that it was obtained as ICTY-Srebrenica related 2.xls. This describes how the list was consolidated. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted). And then duplicates were eliminated and we have ended up with a list which contains -- let me just try and find it, please, bear with me -- 3.947 persons all together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Soljan?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, please, two points. When the witness refers to ICTY-Srebrenica related 2.xls I would like confirmation whether this is actually what we know as the ICMP identified list of October 2007 or some other document. Second of all, if it indeed is the ICMP document, then the names need to be stricken given that it is a document that has so far been admitted under seal and the names have not -- cases haven't necessarily closed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's deal with the first of these. In your previous answer, Mr. Kovacevic, when referring to 2.xls, were you referring to the ICMP list of October 2007? Or were you referring to some other document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We received the list in electronic version. I wouldn't be able to give you an answer to this question. I only know that this -- the -- this was the file name in the electronic version that we received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. One moment. Let me deal with this, Ms. Tapuskovic. Do you have a copy right in front of you of this list now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't have it in front of me because it was in electronic version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If we show you a hard copy of it, would you be able to recognise it? Ms. Soljan?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: It's a rather poor copy, Your Honours, but --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why wouldn't you be able to recognise it, if you have seen it in electronic format?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wouldn't be able to recognise it because in the electronic format, it was provided in the corresponding xls format. My IT expert analysed it, so I wouldn't be able to recognise the list in terms of being able to recognise the names on the list.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can I please add something to this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Madam Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The document was submitted to the witness in electronic form a couple of months ago. We now have it on the computer and our assistant, whom we had introduced yesterday, Mr. Bozo Grbic, has it on the computer and he's working on it now. He could be able to locate it. At the moment of disclosure of this document which arrived several months ago, we did not know that it was under seal. And we don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We still have to identify the document in any case. So that's why I remained -- or we remained in open session because we are still talking in a sort of a vague way, so... Yes, Ms. Soljan?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was just referring to the names that were given by examples by the witness. It would be, I believe, wise to strike them in the event that this is indeed what I assume it is, the number 3002 exhibit, but pending confirmation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So Madam Registrar, if you could go to page 21, please, last -- you can start from page -- line 24 on page 21, to the first word in line 2 on page 22. And redact those, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if there is need for us to refer to any of the tables containing names, we shall go into private session, but I don't think it will be necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to the same document, to the previous table therein. It is table number 1 on page 10 of the report. Mr. Kovacevic, you explain here why, in column containing the number of missing, we have number 7.659. All these figures in the table, do they comprise only the civilian population or not?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These figures were listed on the basis of the documents which are identified in the report under Roman 3 in the annex. I took the figures from the documents dated January 1994, the 1991 census, 11 January 1995, and 11 January 1994. I took these figures as being relevant. According to these documents, this number of population contains also the troops which were present in the protected area of Srebrenica before July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you explain the role or the function of the last column, which reads, "Balance," and in brackets, "S-R"?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last column titled, "Balance S-R," in brackets provides the difference between the appropriate number of inhabitants according to a given document, and the ascertained number of displaced persons on the basis of the documents and records we received from the ICTY and which were described herein in the annex under paragraphs 41, 42 and 43. The difference shows the mathematical number of missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The mathematical value you state in the first row under the column "balance," 2.988, what does it indicate?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The difference of 2.988, has the highest value of all the differences ascertained on the basis of the documents showing the numbers of inhabitants and displaced persons, which shows that on the basis of these documents, this number cannot be brought into correlation with the number of missing, which is this 7.661, and that the actual number of displaced persons remains at the level of the value we have here, which is 2.988.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let us dwell a bit on column 4, which has the designation, "R" and which stands for the number of displaced persons. All the four rows state the figure of 34.537. Can you tell us how is it that you arrived at this particular figure of the displaced persons?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This number was arrived at through a mathematical processing of four documents in electronic format which were listed in paragraph 41. The first document - let me not read the designation of the document, you have it in the paragraph - contains 9.258 persons. The second document contains 4.816. The third document contains 6.116 persons. And the fourth document, 2.832 [as interpreted] persons. All these documents were dated as after July 1995 and they all have the expression saying, related to the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Just let me stop you there. On page 25, line 21 of the transcript, you said the third document -- or rather the fourth document. What was the number?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By merging these four documents, one database was made. The first document was dead, in IT terms, so first it was revived and then the four documents were merged, resulting in a single database. This was done in such a way where that only those persons were taken into account which had next to their name stated as the year of their displacement 1995. Next, duplicates were eliminated of persons appearing in both or all of the documents, and the persons who had the same first and last name, parents' name and year of birth were considered to be one and the same persons. Thus, the figure of 34.537 individuals was arrived at, which is in the database, and this is considered to be the lower threshold or the lower limit, since it's quite possible that some displaced persons had not been registered or had otherwise been left out in these documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This figure of 34.537 is considered to be the minimum number of displaced persons by you?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We consider this figure to be the minimum number of displaced persons on the basis of these four documents that were available to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 31 of your report, you refer to soldiers and the number of soldiers present in the protected area, as well as about the number of soldiers pulled out, and they were labelled as "PV." Can you tell us how it was that you processed the data you received concerning the number of missing soldiers which was the number of 2.895?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This involved two documents mentioned in paragraphs 51 and 52, which give the number of soldiers in the protected area of Srebrenica at 6.000. I will omit mentioning the name of the number of the document. And as for the number of soldiers who pulled out of Srebrenica, that figure is 3.105. Now, the difference between the two figures gives us the number of the missing soldiers that is being referred to here.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have document P3472 called up in e-court, please? Can we scroll down, please? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic, are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is one of the two documents I refer to.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document which refers to a number of which soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The number I am mentioning here, the members of units.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Under 1, we have the defence liberation unit involved in combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now call up document P3470? Can we please turn to page 2, or, rather, the last page of the document?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic, can you please read for us the information concerning the author of the document?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see the bottom. Oh, you mean --

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The heading.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "Command of the 2nd Corps" -- or rather, "the BiH army, 2nd Corps, command of the 28 Division."

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What were the conclusions you made on the basis of the document you have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My conclusion was that the total number of men recorded after the fall of the protected area of Srebrenica, as members of the military units of Srebrenica, was 3.105.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us go back to document 1D1129. Let's turn to the table on page 10 of the B/C/S version. Mr. Kovacevic, column number 5 of table 1 from your report is titled, "Number of those identified or capital I in brackets" and we can see that this number of 3.947 individuals appears in each and every one of these rows. What is the significance of this number of persons identified for this particular table and your report as a whole?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to the number of soldiers who pulled out of the protected area of Srebrenica, according to the document we looked at a moment ago, this particular number here has been placed in the context of the balance which stands for the difference between the number of inhabitants and the number of displaced persons. I've already said, when I was mentioning indicative numbers, that out of the number of persons identified, 3.947, if you take -- if you deduct from that number the number of 1.300 individuals who got killed, then we arrive at the number of 2.647, which is the balance, which stands for the difference in the number of inhabitants and the number of the displaced persons. One can arrive at the same result where one looks at the number of soldiers who were not recorded as having pulled out, which is, in fact, the figure of 2.895. In the context of the balance, a possibility emerged to the effect that the actual, real number of missing persons is, in fact, part of that military unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can we look at document 1D1139? Mr. Kovacevic, can you tell us who authored the document and who it is addressed to?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document was made by the municipal staff of the civilian protection of the municipality of Srebrenica on the 10th of January 1994 and was signed by the president of the Presidency of the Srebrenica municipality, Fahrudin Salihovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can we now turn to page 3 of the document? The bottom half is what we are interested in. Can we turn to the next page, please? Can we please scroll down? Thank you. I will read out a passage from this document to you. "Moreover, due to the war activities in the area of the municipality of Srebrenica, around 1.300 individuals have been killed so far whose identities have been established and who have been buried in cemeteries that are already in existence and in eight newly established cemeteries." Mr. Kovacevic, when you referred to 1.300 soldiers, was this the document you had in mind that I'm just showing to you?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What is, then, your general conclusion, in view of the balance you arrived at in table 1 and the results of the cross-referenced documents that were the subject of your analysis?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A general conclusion would be that the actual number of missing persons on the basis of the sources and data available ranges between 3.000 -- or rather is within the interval of 3.000 and that the data available and the documents available do not allow for a number to be arrived at which would correspond to the number of missing persons found on the list, which is 7.661.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that this would be the right time for our break, although I only have need of some ten minutes more to examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will have the break now. 25 minutes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, for the record, the Prosecution side has now also Mr. Christopher Mitchell, in addition to Mr. McCloskey and Ms. Soljan. And I notice that Mr. Krgovic's son is absent. He went out to change his jeans, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, I think he's had enough of keeping an eye on me today, Your Honour. He's gone to enjoy the sunshine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't blame him. Yes, Madam Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Just a brief remark. During the break, the witness handed over all of the papers that he had in front of him during the testimony. Among the papers is the report drafted by the witness, as well as some certain tables, which is document 380, containing the 71 criteria and the notes he prepared for himself to testify. Unless the Chamber thinks otherwise, I believe it may not be necessary to go in every detail through the notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, if there is any problem with it, then by all means, it should be read out loud.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Not unless we hear more submissions on the topic. So let's proceed with your next few questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 37 of your report, Mr. Kovacevic, you mention the possibility of creating imaginary persons. Can you explain what did you mean by non-existent persons?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 37 has to do with an approach when using letters. In the lists, such as the compiled list.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Not lists but scripts.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What happened is that certain Latinic letters with diacritics, these being [B/C/S letters spoken], were replaced by C, Z, S and D, which had an impact on the numerical information -- excuse me non-numerical information, such as first and last name, father's name, place of disappearance, place of birth. In this way, what we can have are persons who do not appear on any documents or registers, such as the census or the voters' register.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You said that it could have a great impact on the process of identification. Can you tell us what percentage we are talking about when discussing the names from the former Yugoslavia or from Bosnia-Herzegovina, how many names contain such letters with diacritics?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many names from the territory of the former Yugoslavia contain these signs with diacritics which are characteristic of the Croatian Latinic script. I cannot give you a percentage. It would require a separate onomastic research on my part.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could we please have 1D312 put up in e-court? Mr. Kovacevic, can you tell us who the author of the document is. Could we zoom in, please so then the witness would be able to read.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The heading is, "The Statistics Institute of Bosnia-Herzegovina" with the headquarters in Sarajevo. This is the branch office in Tuzla, as well as the regional Defence Secretariat in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the document?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please go down the page. Yes. This document talks about the number of inhabitants in the protected area of Srebrenica, the date --

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Please go back to the top of the page so as to be able to see the date.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it is the 11th of January 1994. Yes. It is referred to in table 1 of my report, in the last column, where it says, "Date." It is the document concerning the number of inhabitants, the number being 37255. Moreover, what is of particular importance for the analysis is the fact that this document categorises the population in the categories of locals or displaced persons within the protected area of Srebrenica or those who moved into the protected area of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could we please go back to the bottom of the document? Thank you. Mr. Kovacevic, talking about this document, you mentioned the figure of 37255. How did you arrive at that figure? Because we don't see it in the document.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simple math. When you add up the numbers contained therein, 9791, 10756 and 16708.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What is your understanding of the remark in the document? I will read it out for you. "The requested data is attached or contained for your statistical research. You should not provide this material to international organisations because our calculations vary by some 45.000 inhabitants." How would this tally with -- in relation to the information you've provided us with so far?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the remark, I carried out a selection of all documents in which there is any mention of the number of inhabitants in the period before the PA of Srebrenica fell. That is to say, I used this remark to do away with certain numbers mentioned in certain documents, which, in my report, are referred to in paragraph 38. It includes reports sent to international humanitarian organisations in which there are numbers ranging from 43.000 or 42.000 and 40.000. The numbers as such are not specified or broken down in the documents. We have round figures and are obviously blown up due to the remark mentioned here. Therefore I limited myself to the documents and numbers that provide a clear structure and that are authentic and signed and that provide with the number of citizens as stated in table 1 in lines 1 through to 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: We will have a look at the documents you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 1D1197 brought up in e-court?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic, do you see the document?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the date is?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 19th of June 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Who was it sent to?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an intelligence report forwarded to the 2nd Corps command in Tuzla, intelligence department.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let us please go down to the last paragraph next.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the document that you based your calculation on that is mentioned in your report whereby you mention 43.000 inhabitants in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only referred to this number. However, I did not use it in my calculations. I rejected it to come up with a total for the reasons I've explained concerning the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Please go to 1D1142 next. Let us go to page 2 -- no, first of all, Mr. Kovacevic, can you tell us what the date of the document is?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 15th of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hmm. Yes, I'm familiar with the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can we go to page number 2? In paragraph 5, line 7, the figure of 42.000 inhabitants of Srebrenica is mentioned. When you were drafting your report, you mentioned the figure. Did you have this document in mind?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had in mind this particular document, although the document itself says that this figure was not confirmed. It was established in 1993 but never confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: We have just mentioned a document that speaks about the humanitarian aid and how the number of 45.000 inhabitants of Srebrenica was used to calculate the quantity of humanitarian aid. Can you tell us on what basis was humanitarian aid handed out?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have a particular document that would with provide the precise criteria for the delivery of humanitarian aid but it is only normal to assume that the humanitarian aid was always calculated on the basis of the number of inhabitants of an area.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, now we are going to ask our assistant, Mr. Bozo Grbic, to display on our screens, but not in the gallery, just in the courtroom, to display the 1991 census as processed by the team that participated, together with Mr. Kovacevic, in the drafting of the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mr. Kovacevic, do you see it on your screen?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, column that is now bolded, what does it represent?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The column's title is, "JMBG" which is the abbreviation standing for the personal identification number.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What you've just told us --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Could we just get the exhibit number for this?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just bear with me for a moment, please. This is Exhibit number 1D1196, and for my learned friends in the Prosecution, this is the electronic database which is the result of the work of the expert and his associates in the Tribunal's demographic department.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please confirm what you've already told us when explaining the meaning of the personal identification number, that the 0s that we are seeing marked in a large number of cases actually show that the ID number is incomplete?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There are such examples of things missing from the personal number. This happens because the person who is taking the census sometimes does not have available to them some of the personal documents such as ID or passport or anything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And now could we please call up the same document in e-court but only its part relative to the list of voters? And we would also like the document not to be shown to the gallery. Mr. Kovacevic, in my -- in answering my question, you said that the register of voters also contained the personal identification number.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Looking at this random sample that you see before you at the moment, are the personal ID numbers complete here?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they are not complete here. However, when it comes to the list of voters, these numbers should be complete - now we have them complete in this part that I see now - because the voters are registered based on their ID document which in this case is a personal ID card.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If we look at the third column from the left, which is envisaged to contain the name of the person's father; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What can you tell us about the characteristics and quality of the list of voters which do not contain the father's name?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The quality is insufficient because the father's name is a very necessary element of the person's identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can we now see the results of the matching according to Brunborg's criteria for which you said that the results were not delivered to you? Let's now use criterion number 27 for the matching process. The matching process here was carried out between the census and the missing list. Please look at your report, Mr. Kovacevic. Can we now see Exhibit 1D1129 in e-court, please? Page 6. There is a table on page 6 which I would like to call up. I would like to display criterion number 27. Thank you. In the second column here, what number of candidates did we arrive at?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the second column?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the column that refers to the census. 4.761.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Can we now go back to 1D1196? And can we ask Mr. Grbic to display the 27th criterion again? Mr. Kovacevic, could you please read for us the number that appears as the result of the matching according to that criteria?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This is the same number that you mentioned --

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number has been transported from here.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And now I would kindly ask the assistant to display the table which was achieved based on the use of the 42nd criterion that you called least stringent criterion?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the least stringent.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us the number of candidates according to this matching process did you receive in column 2?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And the same refers to the column in the census according to all the matches?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at your own table, which you have before you, this is table 1, how many persons may be taken into consideration from the census with only one matching criterion?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With only one candidate in the census for the given person in the list of missing, the number is 6.958.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Kovacevic. We will no longer need the tables. Now I'm going to ask you another question. What would be your final comprehensive conclusion? What is the quality of Brunborg's 71 criteria and what can we say about the quality of the list of missing persons?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the 71 criteria are concerned, this group of criteria is so extensive and so comprehensive that actually it all -- there is almost no person in the list of missing persons or in any other list for that matter that could not be found in the census if we applied these criteria. As for the second part of your question, could you please repeat that.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The quality of the list of missing persons?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the quality of the list of missing persons, this quality can be judged as poor quality, and the problem of matching as carried out by Brunborg and Urdal when we they matched the census and the list of missing persons in order to approve the trustworthiness of this list lacks documentation to -- on which it is based, i.e. the relations between the persons have not been incorporated in the triangle census, list of missing persons, list of voters.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness and it has brought my examination-in-chief to an end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sarapa, yes, he's also your witness. Do you plan to put questions to him?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no questions for this witness, as everything that we were going to ask has been exhausted so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic for the Beara team?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We have no questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bourgon. Mr. Gosnell?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: No questions, Mr. President, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a few questions, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you've just given the total number of inhabitants in Srebrenica, and in your report at page 8 in English and page 10 in B/C/S, we find that you refer to a document dated January 1995, according to which at the time there were 36.051 inhabitants in Srebrenica. According to your research, is that figure of inhabitants similar to the one of -- to the number of people who were in the Srebrenica enclave in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I would like to show you Exhibit P515. This is a report prepared by the United Nations. Let me explain that whilst the document is being pulled up. It's a document dated 13th of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have point 6 on the screen, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: According to point or to item 6 of this report, 50 babies were born yesterday, in other words, on the 12th of July. And to give you the proper picture of this document, we are talking here about Potocari where part of the population of Srebrenica had gone in July 1995. In your expert opinion, is it possible that out of a population of roughly 36.000 inhabitants, is it possible to have 50 babies born on a given day?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Starting from the number of inhabitants, which is 36.051, under the assumption that all the population was in Potocari that you have just referred to, 50 babies in one day would mean that over a period of one year, over 18.000 babies are either born or can possibly be born, which would then mean that every fertile woman would have one and a half baby a year, which is absolutely impossible. There are no such populations anywhere in the world.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Fauveau. Mr. Josse?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And that leads us -- brings us to you, Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: My name is Lada Soljan and I am an attorney for the Prosecution at the ICTY. Now, we haven't met before; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And we haven't discussed this case or any aspect of your report?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: You have met with the Defence counsel, however?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: I'm asking, on how many occasions have you met with the Defence counsels all together?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're referring to the lawyers? Over the period of three years of my work on this analysis, I've met with them a number of times but I wouldn't be able to tell you exactly how many times.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And of course in the course of your meetings with the Defence counsel for Mr. Popovic, you have discussed your report with the attorneys?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Different documents, different -- the contents of all these different reports, the databases, the information that I required for my work, and little by little, we did arrive at the final report, i.e. I drafted the final report and then, in preparation for my testimony here, we obviously discussed that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And therefore you discussed the substance of your testimony with them?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course we discussed the form of my testimony, the contents, the possible questions, documents, the trustworthiness of those and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And in fact, today during your testimony you were referring to a document that was produced in the course of your discussions with the counsel; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are we talking about here? I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: What I mean to say is besides your own report which you had at your desk over there, you also had the 71 criteria of Mr. Helge as Ms. Tapuskovic has said, in addition to that you also had you two sets of notes, one sort of a key set of notes with the main figures as well as a about a 13, 12-page document which contained the questions that were going to be discussed in the course of your direct testimony today; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not entirely correct. The outline of the questions contained some of the questions, not all of them, but also it contains some of the questions that we assumed or rather I assumed that would be put to me but in the course of my testimony have not been put so that these questions were noted with my own hand on the paper and I just drafted my possible answers. This would have served me to avoid wasting time, although my answers were actually much broader than just -- than the notes that I made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I object to this line of questions about the notes because immediately after the break, we suggested that these notes be read in the courtroom and that everybody be informed about their contents. We are now in the sphere of speculation, so I suggest that the notes be read so that everybody can see exactly what they contained. We suggested that this be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Soljan?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wouldn't say I agree quite with the characterisation that Ms. Tapuskovic gives to this. It was according to your order that we gained access to the notes. I simply wanted to make this. There is no speculation. I'm not going any further with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed. Let's proceed. And let's go to the substance of the -- what Mr. Kovacevic's testimony should all be about.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kovacevic, in the course of your preparation for your testimony today as well as for your report, you had an opportunity to also review related testimony; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only one, which I have here in the binder. I looked at it and I believe that was the testimony provided by Brunborg and Urdal.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. But --

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm right. On the 1st of February and the 9th and 10th of May 2007, Brunborg testified and I have that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: All right. So you've reviewed Mr. Brunborg's testimony from this trial. Did you review any further testimony?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not that I remember. I may have come across something over the three years of my work but I can't remember. But in any case, even if I have seen something, it still isn't of any major relevance for my report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. But just to be clear, so you did not review the testimony of Dr. Ewa Tabeau from 5th February of this year, 2008?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not reviewed that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Nor did you review the testimony of Dr. Thomas Parsons from February 1 of this year?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And did you review any of the testimonies of the forensics experts who have testified in this case, such as Jose Baraybar, John Haglund, John Clark, Richard Wright, Christopher Lawrence, all of whom testified early 2007?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These days, Professor Dunjic, has given me a copy, but I'm not sure whether this is his testimony. The number of the document is IT 0588.
