The only thing I was interested in was the number of persons who, based on the post-mortem and DNA analysis, which are typical of forensic medicine, provided a comment which shows that based on three criteria, we have numbers of 2626 persons, 2553 persons and 3479 persons. I'm not a forensics expert so I'm not well-equipped to analyse this report, but I was interested in that because these figures correspond very well to the numbers that I am talking about, and they are very indicative.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. But so you haven't reviewed -- you have not reviewed any of the testimonies that I've listed for you before?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the testimonies that you've mentioned, I have not seen two.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. I believe the correct number would be more than that because I mentioned Dr. Ewa Tabeau's testimony, Dr. Parsons as well as the testimony of about six forensic experts who testified.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right there. I apologise. As far as the forensic reports are concerned I can't tell you anything because I'm not an expert in the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. Now, in order to refer to -- in order to prepare and review relevant documents for your own report, you referred to in the course of your testimony today to the February 2000 report by Mr. Brunborg and Mr. Urdal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Have you also looked at other reports besides the 2000 report of Mr. Henrik and Mr. Urdal, sorry, Mr. Brunborg and Mr. Urdal?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the annex to his report and Mr. Helge Brunborg's testimony. I have not had at my disposal any other reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. So you haven't seen any of the reports that have been issued in 2005, 16 November 2005, as well as 21st of November 2005?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Nor did you have an opportunity to read the reports that were issued as updates to that, including the testimony of Dr. Ewa Tabeau, well, the basis for Dr. Tabeau's testimony, those would be the 2007 progress report on the DNA-based identification by ICMP which is an update to the 16 November 2005 list?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, an hour ago the witness said that he had received from Ewa Tabeau the most recent report containing 6.661 persons as missing in the demographic unit. The number is 7661.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The most recent list.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The most recent list from the month of April. And the witness said that to the Prosecutor's objection which was to the fact that we didn't know what document the witness was talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Soljan?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: That's a fair comment. I was talking about the reports, though, so far. I was not talking about lists and I'll be very happen happy to refer to specific exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's be clear about this, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Will do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Kovacevic, you have not had a chance to review, as you said, the report dated 16 November 2005. This for the record is Exhibit number 2413. And I can show it to you. I have a B/C/S version of this document printed out.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The document as such is something I did not receive. However, in the demographic unit, I had a list of 7661 at disposal and I used that as the basis of all my analyses.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: But there would be --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mrs. Tapuskovic's microphone be turned off, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Tapuskovic, if you could turn off your microphone? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: But if you're dealing with -- if you have access to the most newly issued list of individuals missing, would you not want to also look at the report and read the methodology that's laid out in the most recent report?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. Of course, I began studying the 2000 report quite some time ago, and in that report I could see the basic methodology. I believe that could not have been changed and it was not until the latest figure of 7661. What is still being used is the matching against the census, the voters' register. I received both. The documents I used are still being used today. I don't see what any new report could change in my findings. However, I would be very curious to see this report in particular, but by sheer coincidence, it didn't get to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: In the course of your testimony, though, I understood that you had been in contact with the Defence counsel for the last three years, so this was not one of the documents that you received from counsel?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And so if -- would you be surprised then to find out that in the 2005 version, as well as the upcoming versions or updates of the reports issued by the demographic unit, they are taking into consideration not only the 1997 and the 1998 voters' register but also the 2000 voters' register?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I must confess that would not surprise me. However, I do not see what one can gain from that because that register is further away from the events than the registers in 1997 and 1998. Therefore, it is not as good to be used as the other two, particularly in view of the fact that the persons from the missing list were not on the voter registers later on. However, what I would find surprising would be if the voters' register from 1996 was used.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Why would you be surprised about that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the 1996 voters' register was closer to the events and would be more relevant, having in mind the goal that was -- that they were trying to achieve.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Indeed you testified about this yesterday. You were saying that you know that elections were held in 1996 and -- but you did not know whether they were parliamentary or what type of elections they were, and you testified that you have no explanation for that, why those elections were not used by the OTP demographic unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Now, in the report which you reviewed, the February 2000 report, this would be Exhibit number P00571, at page 9 -- if we could get those called up on the screen, please? Sir, you should be able to see a B/C/S translation of this document. I'm just going to give you an indication for what this document is. It should be the next page in the B/C/S version, please. Thank you, sir. Now, if you look at the second paragraph of this document, the second sentence of there paragraph says, "[Interpretation] However, registering as such for the 1996 elections was not done, and instead of that, what was made use of was the list --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The census.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: -- from 1991." [In English] So in fact you'd actually been able to see the explanation for why the 1996 census was not used, have you not, sir, in the very report that you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I subsequently learned that there were elections in 1996, and I presumed that certain -- a certain voters' register was made. However, it says here that registering for those elections was not carried out and that the census was used instead. This means that they used the census to generate the voters' register. It is unclear, however, why the voters' register was not used for this matching.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Well, sir, would it surprise you to know that there was no unified electronic database such as existed for the OSCE voters' registration for 1997, 1998 and further?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course it wouldn't surprise me. This is additional information I wasn't aware of. I only said that there were elections and that there were voters' registers, and it wasn't clear to me why these were not used in the analysis.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, you've put together a very detailed and technical demographic report which I would like to go over with you a little bit. You've had of course an adequate opportunity to review your report, have you not?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And to check for any errors?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I admit having discovered a few typos subsequently.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: But they do not change the content and the meaning of your report as it is now?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. They do not change the essence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And your report sets out all of the information therefore that you relied on as well as all of the information you considered in preparing it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And in putting together a report like this, you would agree that you have to be neutral?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And you have to fully consider all of the information that is at your disposal?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And you have to scrutinise the information in order to see that it's accurate?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How should I put it? It is not always possible. I cannot go into issues such as whether that official information is correct, as provided by the president of the Presidency of Srebrenica municipality as regards the lists of inhabitants. This would require different expertise regarding the authenticity of the documents and this did not fall under my remit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: But you would also agree with me that it's important to scrutinise the information to make sure that it's complete?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information was incomplete very frequently when this type of analysis is concerned. That's why I referred to many different sources.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: But at the very least, in order to produce your report, you have to ascertain or scrutinise the information to make sure that it's at least sufficient?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, in principle. Of course, the question of analysing information has many aspects.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And you have to see if it's reliable enough to sustain the conclusions that you're actually drawing in it, is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anything that is an official document is what I thought was reliable.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Sir, what do you mean by official document, just to be clear?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say official document, I mean to say that in that document there is a header, a name of a certain institution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: An institution such as the ICRC or something more specific?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anything that is in institutional form, anything that meets the requirements for what I call an institutional subject.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: But you agree with me that it's important that you have to scrutinise the information to make sure that it is reliable in order to sustain the conclusions you draw?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a request which is a must for any researcher.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And this is particularly important in this case because you know that your report is being offered as evidence?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me, it is important for any case, any report, or any analysis. It is important for me as an analyst and expert, for demography, statistics and other relevant issues, in particular here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And although it may be inevitable, it is important in any technical analysis such as yours to avoid assumptions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When talking about statistical and demographic analysis, it is important to stress that something is an assumption. When drawing conclusions in such reports based on informations and presumptions, one needs to specify that, unless it is evident in itself. Any analysis, be it matching, contrasting, indication, contrasting projections, reconstructing history through numbers, all that allows for certain assumptions. However, one needs to stress that they are present.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: But you'd agree with me that it's always better and more accurate to rely on facts that can be established and substantiated?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In science, no. In the world of science, facts can only be plausible explanations as such. When we use a reference framework in processes such as the one discussed here, or, rather, in testimonies which needn't necessarily be expert testimonies, one needs to insist on facts alone, without assuming or using indications. Of course, in my report, I precisely referred to documents and facts but I also mentioned indications. I used the word indicia so as to distinguish that from the so-called exact proof or finding.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, in your report, you state that the objective of it is to assess the methods used by Helge Brunborg in his work. That would be at paragraph 2 of your report. And the other objective of your report was to give the expert opinion on the number of people who went missing in Srebrenica in July 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And in order to do that as a demographer, you need to be able to determine whether the people reported to have been missing actually of existed?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a part of the process carried out by Brunborg and Urdal. I replicated the process to a certain extent in the part of it which corresponded to computer matching with the list of inhabitants as a relevant source of information to prove that those persons existed. My conclusion was that that procedure and that type of matching, so to say, are limitless and that in that regard, for any person on the missing list, one can find, using certain rules, an appropriate person in the census.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And you referred to computer matching with a list of inhabitants and the census. What you mean by that is you relied purely on the computer matching, there was no additional visual analysis of the matches obtained? If you could please say yes or no, the record doesn't take it --

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are not of course matching numbers in the census but the matching of the census with the list of missing persons. When I say computer matching, I mean the use of the 71 rules which are relaxed as to -- as compared to the unique key of identification. In my finding, you find it in table 1. As I said on several occasions, I could not replicate the visual identification process, as referred to by Mr. Brunborg using the conservative indicators. What I mean is to say that I could not come up with a particular person that could be exactly and precisely matched with the person from the missing persons list. That is the bottom problem, bottom issue, with the whole procedure, because from my point of view, given the importance of the list of the missing persons and the importance of the process that you referred to yourself, it is very important to document each and every person from the list of the missing persons to see whether the procedure was brought to an end in matching the person with another person from the census, and not only to use the separate groups you may arrive at by using certain rules but rather using the conservative criterion which would identify the person as identical to the person from the census from which we began. From my point of view, this is where science stops. And one needs to go back to the documenting of subjective decisions made by researchers and experts who made the decision as to whether a person existed or not and to see what was the basis of such a conclusion and on the basis of what the researcher said that the person from the list of the missing persons is the person from the census, or to turn it around, to say that that person does not have its match, its pair, in the census. That is to say, if the basic identification elements coincide, why the person in the census was rejected as an identical person or the pair of the person from the missing persons list.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: You do realise, however, that on the other side, a pure computer matching will of course avoid certain mistakes. In other words you will not be able to spot certain mistakes if it's purely the computer that's doing that work; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Computer matching was used here rationally as the first phase in the process of matching, of finding the identical person to that in the census. It means that it was used to reduce the number of potentially identical persons so that, by visual insight, i.e. the conservative criterion, one could choose the person we believe to be identical. In other words, the criteria was not used to avoid mistakes but to narrow down the possible groups and to simplify visual identification in terms of time and concentration. For example, imagine someone searching for a -- for someone from the missing persons list out of the 4 plus million inhabitants. Therefore, they looked for those people who, under certain elements, and in the criteria the elements are -- vary from the least to most stringent, in order to arrive at groups which would be included in the visual identification process. Based on the reports, I cannot presume the size of work that needed to be done in order to find a certain person even in such a narrowed down figure such as the figure of 118.000.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And in fact, sir, as you're aware, since you have read Mr. Helge Brunborg's testimony and have been reading at least his 2000 report, this work, the painstaking work has been taking place since at least 1998 so this is a period of about ten years of work including computer matching as well as visual analysis, but I'll move on. And basically you are taking issue with the methodology of the demographic unit but in your own expert opinion, you're trying basically to assess the same issues, how many people were alive once, how many people may be dead or missing?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are two completely different goals and approaches. I dealt with the numbers from the documents, That is to say, how many people used to be alive, how many people were dead. I could not go into the derivation of lists. I dealt with this problem and the methodology used by Urdal and Brunborg. This list derivation is something I find poorly substantiated by documents and methodologically unfounded when talking about transparency and clear indications to show how a certain person from the list was found in the census or why a certain person from the voters' register was rejected as being identical, however many identification elements did match.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And indeed according to your own calculations of the Brunborg's missing persons list, and that would be the updated Brunborg missing person list, as well as the census of 1991, with the census of 1991, you arrive at a number of 2.943 persons who are missing. This would be paragraph 27 of your report.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the report, it is but one of the six indicational calculations. I stressed that on several occasions. I called this an indicational calculation as opposed to what I believe to be a proof in the sense of it being undisputable. I used the most stringent criterion that one can use to match the list of the missing persons and the census. That criterion is not as stringent as the unique key because it does not contain the place of birth but just the basic items like first and last name, father's name and year of birth. Under that key, under that identification process, I arrived at this number of 2943. This number is only an indication because it should be viewed in the context of other indications, that is figures. The number in itself does not represent the number of the missing persons, but it indicates to a possible number of missing persons in the context of other indicational figures which were arrived at by other means, and I showed this here in a separate part of the report referring to the six indicational calculations.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And this number, the actual list of these -- the people that you say is the final list obtained through your conservative or sensible criteria has not -- we, at least the OTP does not have access to that. Was it appended to your report?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's actually in the electronic form with my assistant, just like the comparisons. We have all those in electronic form.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: We would like the Defence for Mr. Popovic to just concretely indicate where on the two CDs the work product of this exhibit, the tables are, and we would like to actually obtain the list of names that was obtained through this matching of the Brunborg list with the 1991 census, please. It doesn't need to be immediately. We would just like to know in the course of today. Thank you. Just one quick comment about this comparison, then we are going to go into these other six indicative results you were talking about or at least a selection thereof but one thing that occurs to me is the census of 1991 contained the data that you use with your sensible criteria, you have the name, the last name, the father's name and the year. Now, often, however -- well, I won't say often but there will be situations where the father's name may be taken down in a sense of not in the nominative case of the name but in the genitive case of the name and as a result of this -- I'm sorry, the record did not pick up your yes, so if you could say it for the record?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, excuse me, what was your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: In the census, in the 1991 census, there are situations where the father's name, for example, will not be purely set out in the nominative case, let's say Ramiz, but it will set out in the genitive form of the case or of the name, which will make it into Ramiza; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You're right, although this is very few and far between in a census because there is a rule and there are separate lines for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: There are, but you have found surely that there are situations where genitive will be applied?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And therefore the actual word will be different. Therefore when you're applying your four sensible criteria if you're applying one name, the nominative form of the name, that will be discarded and would therefore be automatically disregarded by the computer matching process, will it not?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, let's go to some of the data that you were analysing in detail. You were already talking about the table at page 10 of your report in the B/C/S version. And you discussed what you based -- what documents you based your analysis of these documents on. This would be page 10 of the B/C/S and page 6, and this would be Exhibit 1D1129.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are we talking about, table 1? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And there, in table 1, you -- in the very first column, you refer to a document about the number of inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To any document that in one way or another specified a -- specifies the number of inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And these documents are in fact specifically referred to in your report and you discussed them today in testimony with Ms. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And you included in your report and in this table the particular numbers as representative of the number of inhabitants because, as you say at paragraph 31, they were very close and faithfully documented?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In paragraph 32? What paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, 31.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: You say --

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that they are faithfully documented, not in detail. You said in detail and it says faithfully documented here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: I think this may have been an interpretation issue.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The significance is different because details means that I would have detailed analysis of the population structures in my report, but here we are talking about the faithfulness of the documents such as they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: All right. And in fact you didn't include in your table 3 of the documents which you discuss later on because -- and those were documents that contained estimates of 43.000 inhabitants of Srebrenica, 42.000 and 40.000 persons or inhabitants in Srebrenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I've explained all that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: In fact, today in testimony you said they were blown up or unconfirmed. Now, you did, however, list in your table, as we can see, four remaining documents and they are listed separately in order to establish or give an indicative idea of the numbers of Srebrenica individuals between 1995 -- or between January 1991 and 1995.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And you listed them separately because, in your expert opinion, each of these documents provides separate and independent corroboration of the likely number of individuals before the fall of Srebrenica in 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And these numbers as we read them out then are all in the range of about 37.000, they begin with 37525, 37211, 36051 and 37255 and -- is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: You relied on four documents as the basis of your calculation, four separate and independent documents as the basis of your calculation?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean documents referring to the number of displaced persons, the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Now, if we could get on e-court, please, document number 1D312. Is it possible also to get document P3471 side by side? Or if not, I could also put it on ELMO and -- Sir, can you tell us -- can you take a quick look at both of these documents, please, and tell us what the date of them is?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They bear the same date.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us who signed these documents or the two documents?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fahrudin Salihovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And in fact, sir, these are the same documents, are they not?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, these are not the same documents because --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But first of all, these are copies.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: But if you take a look at the numbers, let me just walk you through the numbers here. First of all, it says [Interpretation] Number of local population in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the figures are the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact, the sentence at the bottom and the figures are all the same; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And when you add them up, it should be 37.255; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 55, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay, sir, now, if I can show to you that actually document 1D312 is a document that you cite to in paragraph 37, fourth subparagraph. In fact, the document on the right is the document that you refer to in paragraph 37 --

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... 37.525 rather than 225. Can you tell us now?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: In paragraph 40 it's the same document?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is. It is, yes. It is a typo, although I did not see before. Instead of 5, it should be 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: But you'd agree --

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it does not change the essence of the bottom line.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay, sir, but when we go back to table 1, in fact, we had mentioned just previously or you had mentioned to us that there were these four separate lines which created six indications of how many individuals were living in Srebrenica somewhere between 1991 and 1995, in fact, one whole row of your -- or two whole rows are in fact the same row, they are the same document or based on the same document? Let me make it even clearer. In paragraph or rather table 1 on page 10 you refer to a number, a total number of inhabitants which is 37.525, that's your very first number, your very first S number, and the last row of your document of the table 1 cites to 37.255?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... both these documents are January 1994?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... same numbers, same date, same last name or same signature of the person, it is indeed the same document?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that this is the same document, although I treated them as two different, but this is because of the typo in the first column, instead of 5 it should be 2 but this does not really change the story about indicative numbers because only one indicative number has been derived from this table. The number here is 2.998 as the uppermost limit. However, because of the error it should be lower, it should be 2.718.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. But in short, your table should contain only 3 and not 4 references to the Srebrenica population?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is how it seems at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can we go back to P03471 for a moment, please? Now, sir, in relying on these figures, in relying on these figures, you did not consider any additional data, did you, the figures that are set out in this document?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was referring to the number of population, no. I -- when I was referring to this particular number, 37.255, I could not use anything else because this is the figure that was referred to within this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay, so the document and the numbers did not come with a list of names attached to it?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see any such lists.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And the document did not contain a list of JMBGs or anything similar?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I say, I did not have any such list of names. I can't even assume that they exist or not. I don't believe that they exist as statistical records but I believe that the figures were compiled based on some register and they were then used by some local authorities. That's where -- the way they were compiled in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do have a fair bit more to go. I don't know if this would be the right time to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's time anyway. So let's have a 25-minute break. Do you think you'll finish your cross-examination today?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do we need to keep the next witness here or not, if he's here, Madam Registrar, I don't know if he's here or not. You will check and in the meantime, you and Madam Tapuskovic will liaise with the registrar and just make sure that the gentleman, if he's here, will not stay here unnecessarily. So 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Now, earlier in your testimony, you told us that you had excluded numbers of Srebrenica population -- three documents with numbers of Srebrenica population that numbered 40.000, 42.000, 43.000 persons.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Yet the documents that you did rely on contained no names, no list of names, no list of JMBG, no kind of verifying information that would allow you to actually rely on that data; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within this context, within the context of reliability, which you have emphasised just now, what matters is the administrative reliability and not the issue of statistical demographic or any other research of reliability, the reliability of the figures contained in the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay, sir, but you'd agree with me that a document coming directly from the Srebrenica statistical organisation would be as relevant as a document coming from UNPROFOR, for example, and you've relied on documents both from Srebrenica as well as from United Nations?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. A document coming from the statistics department, i.e. from the president of the Presidency of the municipality, and is sent to the statistics department, is relevant because its subject is the number of inhabitants. If we are talking about an UNPROFOR document, then you can see that this document is not intended for establishing the number of inhabitants. It is just a bypass product. And in one place it is even identified as unverified. So these numbers of inhabitants in a document like this have not been checked. They have been rounded off to a round figure. And they don't rely on any official document provided by local authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay, sir, but you'd agree with me that the documents we were just discussing before break do not contain any lists, they do not contain any kind of a verifying data attached to them?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not receive any such lists, but this doesn't mean that in the background of the document and the administration behind such documents, such as the president of the Presidency of Srebrenica, such documents do not or did not exist. It is fair to assume that such lists did exist because the number of inhabitants is specified in here. Moreover, it is segregated by the categories of local population, displaced population, people who had moved in from elsewhere, and it is obvious that the figures have not been rounded off.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay, sir, but you yourself did nothing to check about the existence of such documents?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must admit that that goes beyond the scope of what I was tasked to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Sir, you testified earlier that you have not actually reviewed the most recent reports produced by the demographic unit of the OTP; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are referring to the written documents and reports that you mentioned, I have not had an opportunity to read them, but I relied on the most recent versions of the list based on which the reports have been compiled.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And therefore, you had access to what is called the Srebrenica missing persons -- or Srebrenica missing persons reported missing and dead after the takeover of the Srebrenica enclave by the Bosnian Serb army on 11 July 1995 and this is the 2007 progress report on the DNA-based identification by ICMP.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand your question, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, there's a document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. It seems to be solved. Ms. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would kindly ask my learned friend from the Prosecution to explain to the witness the meaning of ICMP. This is an abbreviation and I would like if she could explain the abbreviation to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Could you explain the acronym to Mr. Kovacevic, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic, are you aware of the existence of an organisation called international commission for missing persons?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard of that organisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And the acronym for this organisation is ICMP?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well, then.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Now, the ICMP is discussed in the earlier reports of 16th November 2005, 21st November 2005 and in fact we have a whole lot of evidence that has been discussed here in court over the last year and a half that comes from the ICMP. In fact, what we have as of October 2007 from the ICMP is 5.021 individuals who have been exhumed from graves, Srebrenica-related graves, and whose IDs we have from the ICMP. Would it surprise you to know that?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be surprised to hear that. However, this is down to the identification of exhumed bodies and this is something that is outside the scope of my report. I know this is a very complex issue and it is the forensic experts, medical professionals, that do that kind of job.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: But surely you would agree with me [Microphone not activated]--

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Surely you would agree with me that the best evidence of a person being dead, which was part of the equation used by the demographic unit in compiling its missing list, is an actual proof of his death, of his existence in a grave related to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have emphasised that I'm not even familiar, let alone an expert in the issue of body identification. This is part of the science of pathology and I can only logically conclude that an entirely new issue arises here when it comes to the exhumation of bodies and their identification. I do not belong to the profession but I know it is a very delicate and time-consuming job and sometimes it can be very complicated, and obviously there are methods and expert opinions and I'm really not an expert in the area and I'm afraid you will have to talk to somebody who is an expert, so I cannot agree with you that it is sufficient enough to find a body or a grave to confirm that the dead body is actually somebody who is on the missing list.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: But indeed, if you had had access to the documentation that I've listed to you in the course of your testimony here today, you would have realised that yes, it is a complex process but indeed we have had an expert from the ICMP come here and explain to the Court how the -- how the DNA was compiled and how this number has been arrived at, would you not have wanted to look into that evidence in order to consider more the validity of the data before you, the complete data before you?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These days I've had an opportunity owing to sheer coincidence to meet an expert from that field and to arrive -- to get hold of some of the documents that he is privy to, and the documents that I am talking about is -- pertains to the field of pathology and body identification, and obviously I saw a different figure there, different to the 5.021 but I repeat, I cannot talk about that. It is not part of my job. My job boils down to the statistical demographic and record research and not at all to the issue of exhumation and arriving at a figure on that basis. If I had an opportunity to embark on a more complex investigation of the whole issue, then I would love to be a member of the -- of a mixed team that would consist of an expert pertaining to my profession and a pathologist. That team would be a mixed team that would also involve people from the Prosecution, people from the Defence, and such a complex team would work interactively and look at all the facts interactively and would embark on compiling a very complex multi-layered report. In my humble view, that might take years to comply -- to compile.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Sir, I'll -- let me ask you one more thing. Were you also informed by the Defence that the ICMP, as of November 30th of last year, had received DNA data for 7.772 individuals reported to be missing in Srebrenica? If you'd had this data -- well, first of all do you know about the existence of this information?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Tapuskovic? One moment, one moment. Ms. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness on several occasions said that he has nothing to do with identifications, and a little while ago he said clearly that he deals with statistics and demography, which has nothing to do with the identification of bodies, be it classical identification or DNA identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Still, I think the substance of Ms. Soljan's question is directed more to the number that shows up in that document than to anything else and what's being asked of the witness is to know whether he is familiar with this document or not. So he can answer this document -- this question, and then we proceed from there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, I'm not familiar with this document, because I believed that this type of documentation did not fall within the domain that I was supposed to deal with. However, as a person who can of course hold a wider view of the matter, I believe that this type of documentation is not particularly relevant in the context of my research because, in it -- or rather, it implies the issue of expertise concerning identification. I know from such experts that that area is very complex and that various and different experts see this in a different way.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir. But you misunderstood my questions. ICMP on November 30th actually sent us a letter saying they have 7.772 persons reported missing. In other words, it's not a matter of full identification, this is how many profiles they had as of November of persons missing. That's demographic data, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I have not seen such a list. And as far as I can see in the primary report, it was not a reference referred to when drafting the missing persons report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, when you refer to the primary report, what are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The primary Brunborg-Urdal report from 2000.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Well, certainly it wasn't referred to then but there have been updates ever since and the ICMP data has been crucially recognised. The point is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please avoid arguing with the witness and limit yourself to questions, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: What I'm putting to you, though, is if an organisation has a number of individuals reported to be missing, would you not want to maybe have access to this data in order to be able to evaluate this data?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I would like to have them, but then I would carry out a separate research in the sense of matching it with the census and voters' registers and so on and so forth. However, my goal here, my primary goal was not for me to derive or prove that a certain list is good or not, realistic or not. It was up to me to try and bring into dispute that the list produced by Brunborg and Urdal should be viewed in the context of all information that we have and in the context of the methodology used so as to prove that it is not true, that it is not a valid list, and that its validity cannot be corroborated by the documents I had at my disposal.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: But, sir, in your own report you actually referred to ICMP data, data from the ICMP, is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which piece of information you have in mind. Could you please be specific?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: You refer to a document called ICTY-Srebrenica related 2.xls.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: ICTY Srebrenica, the list of identified persons, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And were you aware, when you were making calculations with this document of where this document came from?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably did. I didn't emphasise this in particular. I knew it was an official document in the sense that we received it from the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And it's actually -- the Defence has cited that as 1D1127, but what I'd like to know is did you know therefore that this was a document directly received from the ICMP?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say it was not that relevant for me. It was important for me that we received it via the Tribunal and that in terms of contents, it is a list of those identified. As for our additional computer research, it was so that -- it was done because we wanted to make the list as valid as possible because it was rather problematic in terms of names, duplications and so on and so forth. That's why we went down from 5673 to 3943.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Well, the demographic unit used this very same data received from the ICMP and Ms. Ewa Tabeau has testified about it during her testimony of 5 February 2008, that 6.609 pieces of data had arrived all together on that very list that you were analysing and out of those, 4.263 were identified persons, matched to living family members who had reported their loved ones missing from Srebrenica, so 4.263 were then matched against the list, the missing list, the 7.661 missing list and an overlap of 50 per cent was obtained; 3.837 persons from that list of 4.263 identified persons, 90 per cent from that list are on the OTP missing list, the list containing 7.661 persons.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: The question is shouldn't you have done that with the information you had available?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe the witness should be informed on whether that is disputed by the Defence or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must say that I did not understand the question, or, rather, I don't know whether there was a question. However, what I can say before the question is repeated is that this list that I had at my disposal was matched with the list of the missing by first and last name, name of one of the parents, and year of birth. It is a key which takes into account the elements found in both the list of the missing -- or that is to say the identified and the Brunborg missing list. And the figure arrived at in this way is 2.738, which is something very distinct from what we are now hearing from Madam Prosecutor. In my report I used that as an indicational calculation only, as one of the six I have been mentioning. Of course, by matching that list, which otherwise is of poor quality, the list of the identified, and when I say of poor quality I mean from the aspect of identification, by using a weaker or less rigorous criterion that we derived, that would result in a higher figure probably. The issue in my mind is why the list of identified is so poor, in terms of identification, if the process also included communicating with the families of the missing and if the identifications were conducted by using methods I am not familiar with. The question is why the list was not filtered better, in terms of information, so as to avoid overlaps and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Kovacevic. If the number 5.021 unique, identified individuals coming out of graves is correct, then your number of 3.000 is not correct; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is so, given that or provided that, in the forensic pathology expert report -- and of course all other material facts concerning the time of disappearance, so on and so forth, it is proven that the figure of 5.021 is correct and that it is in relation with the events in the PA of Srebrenica. What I, as a mathematician used to suspect anything and everything, would say is that I do not believe the figure to be correct. Why? Because then I would have to find it necessary to dispute some of the figures that I included in my report in two documents, and this is the number of the population and the number of displaced persons. Based on the documents available, that cannot be done.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. Just one final question. In the notes that we obtained from you during break, we had a chance during the second break to just review them briefly, and we see there that there are a number of questions that are typed out as well as your handwritten notes. However, in a number of instances there are also answers that are typed out and I was just wondering who typed those answers out, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was entered during the preparations I had in Belgrade with the Defence counsel. Some of it was typed by my secretary, some by myself, then I made additions in handwriting, some associations, I received some information from the attorneys. I cannot tell you precisely what was written by whom at what time. We worked in stages.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay, sir, and as I was to see at some points during your testimony, you were able -- you were reading those notes, were you not?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if you noticed that when answering, I was not reading, because I always looked in front of me. However, I did use the notes to remind me of certain things so as not to have to go back to the documents to find out the figures. This was just -- these were just prompts, suggesting in which direction I should go.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Soljan. Ms. Tapuskovic, do you have a re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I'll be brief. I'll finish before today's session, before the end of today's session, and there will be no need for the witness to return.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic, you were asked about the data put forth by several experts, be it DNA experts, anthropologists, et cetera. To what extent do the results of their findings impact the statistical and demographic issues you dealt with in your report?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They cannot impact the demographic, statistical issues, but potentially, if one goes into that type of analysis, in a combined team, their results could cause a reassessment of certain information that we received through official documents and then used in our analysis. We would have to think about why Mr. Fahrudin Salihovic signed the document about the number of missing persons, when others' documents show differently. However, such a research would probably take a decade or so. It is a very complex issue why someone at a certain moment misinformed an official body or why certain documents contain these numbers instead of those, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: At page 48 of today's transcript, you were asked about the methodology of data processing. In relation to that, when and did you review one of Mr. Brunborg's reports? Would the methodology of statistics change within the interval in between the reports or would the methodology remain the same?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the break, I had a look at the report and it only talks about certain details and some very small additions to the list of missing as compared to the original missing list. As regards the methodology, there were no changes. Of course, in my report, we used the lists, the latest versions of the lists, which were used to draft the reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You were also told that a report arrived from the ICMP which states that on the list of missing, there are at least 7.772 persons. Had you known that figure at the moment of writing your report, would that have changed your approach or would that have had an impact on the result of your report?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would not have had any impact on my approach. However, I would be -- would have been able to compare that number with the lists of voters and then I could indicate a total number of matches or mismatches, much the same way we had done it with the previous ICMP reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You were also shown this ICTY Srebrenica-related document.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what we used.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You described it in your report and you said that it was the list of those identified. Would the situation have been any different had you known that this document arrived from the ICMP instead of the Tribunal, for example?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. For me, it's the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kovacevic, to go back to the document referred to several times by myself and my learned friend, Ms. Soljan, it is 1D312, it needn't be brought up on the screen again. We all know what it is. It is signed by Fahrudin Salihovic. You told us that you believed it to be a manipulation of information so as to arrive at a certain figure concerning the registers in various municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must correct you. I did not say that the document was a manipulation of sorts. What I did say is that it points to the manipulation in certain documents that were sent to humanitarian organisations. I intentionally referred to those documents, even without the remark we had studied here, one could see that these were figures that had been rounded off and probably did not reflect the situation in the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us why you believe that this document is reliable, containing the data it does?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it is official and it was sent to the statistics institute, which is an official state body collecting and verifying, to a certain extent, such information. That institution deals with data and analyses data and, of course, it would be difficult for me to understand why someone would want to misinform their statistics institute on the number of population instead of supplying them with hard facts.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Soljan asked you about the list of those identified and how you arrived at the reduced figure from the 5.000 plus referred to in that document. What procedure did you apply? In your report at page 15 in B/C/S, paragraph 48 -- sorry, 49, you said that there was some screening or cleanup and deletion of duplicate names. What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once we noticed that it was a poor quality list, in terms of identification elements, because we frequently had the -- two names for the same person, we mentioned the example of -- well, I don't believe I can mention the name, but on certain occasions, we had two names for the same person in the same line, and buy computer research we realised that they were duplicates. First we did the following. If we had two names for the same person, we made that one person. If there was Miladin and your name, what was your name, I forgot.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mira Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mira. If that was in the same row, we made it into two persons. We had Milorad and Mira or Miroslav, thus maximising the number. The first step maximised the number of those identified, and then we excluded duplications. If we found Miladin Kovacevic once and then came across him again, then we deleted him the second time around. After those two steps, out of 5786 people we arrived at 3949. It was a reasonable thing to do, in terms of computer processing of a list that is unclear.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any indication which would show that Helge Brunborg did the same?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think Helge Brunborg refers to this list. It was not used to draw the list of the missing. As it is stated, they relied on two lists, one of the ICRC and the other of the Physicians for Human Rights. We used this list because we received it. And then we noticed that it also had certain indicational calculations contained therein.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in any of the documents that you reviewed while preparing your report, did you see that Helge Brunborg said that the person under a certain name on the list of missing, he found under the same name on some other list, be it the census or the list of voters?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not come across that. My basic and final objection to the way all the elements were looked at consists in the following: There are no documents, no relations were established within the triangle consisting of the missing persons list, the census and the list of voters. I think that it is the most indispensable thing that should be done, if given such a task, because for every missing person, you have to see whether that person is in the census, just to establish that he actually did exist. And also which person has the identical identification elements, like, for these 222 persons which were rejected, why they were rejected and what criteria were used to reject that person or to accept the person if we are talking about the census. In a nutshell, that would be the foundation of the trustworthiness of this list in the statistical and demographic sense, and documents have to be prepared for every single person regardless of the text, the fact that it would be time-consuming, but let me refer to the Prosecutor's words. This is not a matter of material process but this is a crucial issue regarding the -- what happened in Srebrenica in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: My last question to you, Mr. Kovacevic, is this: You mention the triangle. In your report and in your work recorded on the three CDs, do you show the interaction within the triangle between the list of missing, the census and the list of voters?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the findings that are given in the report can be covered by documents which refer to the matching between the census and the list of voters. I've already emphasised that I could not embark on the visual identification because I did not have any trace of the visual identification carried out by the authors that have been mentioned in this courtroom. Obviously, this part of matching and analysis cannot be complete or, rather, no correspondence can be established in the way the Prosecutor described it with the findings of the forensic experts, pathologists because this could be a separate subject of a separate analysis which would also imply looking at mirroring one against the other and vice versa.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this completes my examination of this witness. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Tapuskovic, for your cooperation. Mr. Kovacevic, we have come to the end of your testimony, assuming that none of my colleagues wish to ask you questions. I wish to thank you for having come over and tried to explain these difficult matters to us, and on behalf of everyone present, I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would also like to thank you for giving me the opportunity to explain my findings with regard this issue, and I am at your disposal for any other tasks you may give me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I think we can -- you would agree to leave the documents for tomorrow. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to leave it until tomorrow, if you're agreeable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I'm definitely agreeable. We stand adjourned, resuming tomorrow at 2.15, like today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 25th day of June, 2008, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.,
